extracted.intended_audience: Early-career researchers applying for an NIAID/NIH K01 Mentored Research Scientist Development Award (PA-16-190)
extracted.subtask_description: Prepare and submit a mentored K01 career-development grant application (PA-16-190) including SF424 forms, project summary/narrative, human subjects protection, facilities/resources, mentorship and career development plans, and required enrollment/inclusion reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow funding opportunity's instructions for application format
rubrics_metrics.description: Always follow your funding opportunity's instructions for application format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although this application demonstrates good grantsmanship, time has passed since the grantee applied. The samples may not reflect the latest format or rules. NIAID posts new samples periodically: https://www.niaid.nih.gov/grants-contracts/sample-applications

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete SF424 (R&R) application form fields accurately and completely
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide required SF424(R&R) fields including type of submission, dates, applicant information, project title, start and end dates, congressional district, estimated project funding, applicant organizational details, and authorized representative signature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By signing this application, I certify (1) to the statements contained in the list of certifications and (2) that the statements herein are true, complete and accurate to the best of my knowledge. I also provide the required assurances and agree to comply with any resulting terms if I accept an award. False statements may subject applicant to penalties (U.S. Code, Title 18, Section 1001). Include any required cover letter and attachments (e.g., M-22_RRSF424_Cover_Letter.pdf).

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Summary/Abstract must summarize aims and significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a Project Summary/Abstract that explains the research aims, the public health problem addressed, the populations/geography studied, and the expected contributions (e.g., quantifying policy/contextual/geographic patterns of HIV Care Continuum outcomes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach Project_Summary.pdf. The summary should succinctly describe Aim 1, Aims 2–3, data sources (NA-ACCORD, CCASAnet), and overall novelty/importance of analyses (e.g., assessing ACA effects using quasi-experimental designs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Narrative/Public Health Relevance statement required
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a Public Health Relevance Statement (Project Narrative) describing the public health importance of the proposed research and how findings will inform policy, interventions, or national strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State how the research will help identify transitions along the HIV Care Continuum that demand improvement, and how results will be of interest/use to epidemiologists, clinicians, and policy makers (ties to National HIV/AIDS Strategy, WHO guidelines, ACA implications).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliography & References Cited included and properly formatted
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a Bibliography & References Cited document listing relevant literature; references including the applicant as author should be indicated (applicant in bold font in this sample).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach M-4_Bibliography.pdf. Cite foundational methods and prior cohort publications supporting feasibility and approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities & Other Resources must document institutional support and available cores
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe facilities, institutional resources, and research cores that will facilitate the project (e.g., conference/meeting space, videoconferencing, Clinical Trials Unit, Epidemiology/Outcomes Unit, Comprehensive Care Clinic, informatics/data warehouse, data management cores).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe personnel, clinic capacity (VCCC patient numbers, satellite clinics), informatics working group, access to electronic medical records and data warehouses, and how these resources support the research and training environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career development and institutional programs described
rubrics_metrics.description: Document institutional career development resources available to the candidate (e.g., CTSD, VPSD, VCTRS programs, mentorship structures) and how they support mentored research training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe didactic training, mentoring apprenticeship, salary/support, and program expectations (e.g., VPSD/VCTRS require candidate to work within mentor's research space and departmental chair commitments). Include metrics used by institutional programs to evaluate success (publication rates, K-to-R conversion, retention).

rubrics_metrics.name: Protected research time commitment (75%) and institutional commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: For K awardees, the sponsoring clinical department chair must commit to provide 75% protected time for research during the award period and support mentor's laboratory activities and candidate transition to independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State departmental commitments explicitly. Failure to meet protected time requirements can result in withdrawal of institutional salary support or K award (as in Newman Society expectations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentorship plan and mentoring committee composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a clear mentorship plan listing PD/PI, mentors, co-mentors, advisors, and mentoring committee members with role categories and institutional affiliations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List roles (e.g., PD/PI, Other (Specify)-Mentor, Co-Mentor, Advisor, Mentoring Committee) and explain how mentors will provide guidance and training. Include frequency and format of mentoring interactions (e.g., meetings, reviews).

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe data sources, cohort inclusion/exclusion, and provenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain which cohorts/datasets will be used (e.g., NA-ACCORD, CCASAnet), inclusion/exclusion criteria (e.g., excluding interval cohorts for certain aims), and data provenance and mapping procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail routine data audits, cohort-level data mapping, generation of standardized labels, documentation of data quality issues, and how datasets will be transmitted to central Data Management/Epidemiology cores for analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data de-identification per HIPAA and specific masking rules
rubrics_metrics.description: State that all data will be de-identified in accordance with HIPAA guidelines before central storage/analysis; include specific masking rules (e.g., 3-digit ZIP codes entered as '000' for areas with resident populations <20,000).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain assignment of unique study identifiers distinct from parent cohort identifiers and any cohort-level survey procedures that will not involve individual subject contact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data security and access controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Document technical and administrative security measures to protect analytic and source data (e.g., domain controller, user access controls, data access restrictions, NFS export control, tape security, virus/malware monitoring).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe server/workstation restrictions, local admin limits, use of SSL for secure data transfer, disabling insecure protocols (telnet/ftp), and group/user access control settings for web-based data management and administrative webpages.

rubrics_metrics.name: IRB review, approvals, human subjects protections, and waiver justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Address human subjects protections: indicate if human subjects are involved, whether project is exempt, IRB approval status/dates, Human Subject Assurance number, and justification for waivers of informed consent if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If human subjects data are de-identified/off-the-shelf, request waivers appropriately from institutional IRB. Maintain current IRB approvals for contributing cohorts and ensure each cohort's IRB oversight remains in place.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of potential risks, benefits, and protections against risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide discussion of potential risks to subjects (or lack thereof), protections against those risks, and potential benefits (direct or indirect) to subjects and others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If data are de-identified, state minimal risks. Explain measures (de-identification, security) that make risks minimal and reasonable in relation to anticipated benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruitment/informed consent procedures and plan for no additional recruitment when applicable
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe recruitment and informed consent approach; if study uses pre-enrolled cohorts and no additional recruitment, state this and explain implications for consent and IRB review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify whether subjects will be re-contacted (in this sample: subjects will not be re-contacted) and note that additional cohort-level information will be obtained from cohort representatives, not subjects directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Women and Minorities reporting and analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Address NIH inclusion policy: state whether there are exclusions based on sex or race/ethnicity, provide preliminary estimates of composition, and present targeted/planned enrollment tables by sex/race/ethnicity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include PHS Inclusion Enrollment Report forms and demographic breakdowns; explain how analyses will examine disparities by health policy, geography, and individual context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Children policy and justification if excluded
rubrics_metrics.description: Address the NIH policy on inclusion of children (<18 years): define children per NIH, state whether pediatric participants are included, and justify exclusion when applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If cohorts pre-enroll adults only, document this as fulfilling exclusionary circumstances and provide rationale why findings may not generalize to children.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHS Inclusion Enrollment Report and correct reporting format
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete the PHS Inclusion Enrollment Report(s) in the required format (note in the sample: 'This report format should NOT be used for collecting data from study participants').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide planned vs. actual (when applicable), enrollment location (domestic/foreign), clinical trial status, and detailed cell counts by sex, race, and ethnicity as required by the form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource sharing / data sharing plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a Resource Sharing Plan indicating how data acquired with NIH funds will be shared and made publicly available (e.g., via peer-reviewed publication or data repositories).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State any exclusions or notes (e.g., application does not request direct costs ≥$500,000 in a single year; no model organisms or GWAS planned). Describe timelines and modalities for data sharing consistent with NIH policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of key biological and/or chemical resources
rubrics_metrics.description: If the study uses key biological or chemical resources, describe plans for authentication and validation prior to use; if none are used, state this explicitly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include an Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources statement (sample: 'Our proposal does not utilize key biological and/or chemical resources; therefore there are none to be authenticated').

rubrics_metrics.name: Candidate selection and evaluation criteria for institutional career-development programs
rubrics_metrics.description: When institutional programs (e.g., VPSD/VCTRS) are described, state selection/evaluation criteria such as quality of mentor and research environment, training credentials of applicant, and quality of the research proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe institutional expectations for awardees (protected time, reporting, mentoring oversight) and metrics the institution uses to monitor program success (e.g., publication rates, grant conversion rates).
